subject: Media Literacy
title: Framing Bias: How Stories Are Told
description: A short lesson to help you apply Framing Bias: How Stories Are Told.

hook.text: 'Tax relief' vs. 'tax cuts for the wealthy.' Same policy. Different frames. Different public reactions.

buildup.text: Framing bias is how the presentation of a story — its angle, language, and context — shapes your interpretation.

discovery.text: Researchers found that describing the same economic data as 'unemployment at 5%' vs. '95% employment' changes opinions.

twist.text: Framing is invisible because it seems like natural storytelling. You absorb the frame without noticing it.

climax.text: Every story has a frame. Recognizing it is the first step to evaluating the story independently.

punchline.text: The frame decides what you see. Question the frame first.

quiz.question: What is framing bias?
options: Using picture frames in news studios
How the presentation and angle of a story shapes audience interpretation
Only showing one frame of a video
